Subject: Follow-up: retention requirements from today's call

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and privacy teams:

- We need a firm answer on PII handling: can Redwood support a zero-retention option for user content (no persistent logs, no stored messages) for our account?
- For service logs/telemetry, Acme needs a shortened retention window of 30 days for troubleshooting, with PII redaction applied.
- Data residency: EU only (eu-west-1).
- Access controls: audit trail for any access, and approval required for any manual e-discovery.

Procurement will also want this documented as an exception in the contract. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps?

Thanks,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: retention requirements from today's call

Camila — thanks for the summary. Technical note / options:

Short answer: feasible with caveats. Two implementation patterns we can offer on Hosted:

Option A — Zero-retention (recommended for maximum privacy):
- Disable persistent request/response logging for this customer at the routing layer.
- Ephemeral processing only: tokens traverse inference runtime without being written to long-term logs.
- Minimal operational traces (error counters, short-lived traces) retained for 24 hours for debugging; we can make access-to-traces gated and logged.
- Requires a signed retention-exception and ops playbook to avoid accidental config changes.

Option B — Shortened logs + redaction:
- Retain structured telemetry and request metadata for 30 days.
- Run a PII redaction pipeline on ingest (regex + ML scrub) to remove obvious identifiers prior to storage.
- Retention and redaction logs stored in eu-west-1.

Residency: both options can be constrained to eu-west-1 via our routing + storage configuration.

Considerations:
- Some infra-level audit logs (for compliance/SOC2) are stored for a longer window (default 90 days) but we can create a scoped view: those longer-term logs are encrypted and access-managed; we can add a note in the exception that access requires a legal/approved request and is limited in scope.
- If Acme insists on absolute zero storage of any telemetry even for 24 hours, we'd advise Private deployment (on-prem or VPC) to eliminate all vendor-side telemetry copies.

I've attached a draft SLA/implementation doc that we can send to Acme (redwood-data-retention-sla.docx). I'll also draft the retention-exception-form once we align.

	64 Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-data-retention-sla.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: retention requirements from today's call

Thanks for the details, Rafael. Compliance position: we can approve an exception with formal controls. Key conditions: 

- Signed retention-exception form (legal sign-off) capturing the exact fields and durations.
- 0-retention for user content (as defined) is acceptable when configured per Option A; we will document the operational safeguards.
- 30-day telemetry retention with PII redaction is acceptable under Option B.
- Longer-term internal audit logs (90 days) will remain encrypted and isolated — access to those logs must be routed through an approval workflow and be limited to specific purposes (security incident investigation, legal holds).
- We require that the exception be added to the contract as an appendix; legal will include language about scope and data residency.

I've uploaded the retention-exception-form for Acme to review. The form includes the fields we need for legal and SOC2 traceability.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Proposal A (Privacy-first, Hosted):
- 0-retention for user content/PII (no persistent storage of conversation content)
- 24-hour ephemeral operational traces for debugging only
- EU-only residency (eu-west-1)
- Requires signed retention-exception (attached) and ops runbook

Proposal B (Operational balance):
- 0-retention for user content/PII
- 30-day retention for telemetry/structured logs with PII redaction
- EU-only residency (eu-west-1)
- Scoped 90-day encrypted audit logs for legal/incident use, access via approval workflow

Attached: retention-exception-form.pdf (for signature) and redwood-data-retention-sla.docx (draft SLA language).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which proposal (A or B) you prefer.
